model.name: PCI DSS v4.0.1 (starter)
model.documentation: The Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard v4.0.1: its twelve requirements under six goals, each realized by an example control applied to the systems in scope. The cardholder data environment is shown with the connected-to and security-impacting systems around it and the segmentation that keeps the rest of the network out of scope, because scope is what decides how much of the standard applies. Requirement numbers are the standard's; titles and summaries are our own words, and the standard itself, from the PCI Security Standards Council, is the reference. Replace the example retailer's systems with your own.

element.name: PCI DSS v4.0.1
element.documentation: Published by the PCI Security Standards Council in June 2024. Applies to every entity that stores, processes or transmits cardholder data or sensitive authentication data, or could affect its security.

element.name: Requirement 1: Network security controls
element.documentation: Network security controls, such as firewalls, restrict traffic into and out of the cardholder data environment, with rules that are documented, justified and reviewed.

element.name: Network security rule management
element.documentation: Example control. Replace with the process or tool that meets this requirement in your organisation.

element.name: Requirement 2: Secure configuration of system components
element.documentation: Every system component is built from a hardened configuration standard, with vendor defaults changed and unneeded functions removed.

element.name: Hardened configuration standards
element.documentation: Example control. Replace with the process or tool that meets this requirement in your organisation.

element.name: Requirement 3: Protection of stored account data
element.documentation: Store as little account data as possible, never keep sensitive authentication data after authorisation, and render stored card numbers unreadable.

element.name: Tokenisation of stored card numbers
element.documentation: Example control. Replace with the process or tool that meets this requirement in your organisation.

element.name: Requirement 4: Strong cryptography in transit
element.documentation: Card numbers are protected with strong cryptography whenever they travel over open, public networks.

element.name: TLS for card data in transit
element.documentation: Example control. Replace with the process or tool that meets this requirement in your organisation.

element.name: Requirement 5: Protection from malicious software
element.documentation: Anti-malware runs on systems at risk, stays current, and is backed by protection against phishing.

element.name: Anti-malware on CDE systems
element.documentation: Example control. Replace with the process or tool that meets this requirement in your organisation.

element.name: Requirement 6: Secure systems and software
element.documentation: Software is developed securely, vulnerabilities are found and patched by risk (critical patches within one month), and scripts on payment pages are controlled.

element.name: Secure development and patching
element.documentation: Example control. Replace with the process or tool that meets this requirement in your organisation.

element.name: Requirement 7: Access by business need to know
element.documentation: Access to system components and cardholder data is granted only to those whose job needs it, and reviewed.

element.name: Role-based access to card data
element.documentation: Example control. Replace with the process or tool that meets this requirement in your organisation.

element.name: Requirement 8: Identification and authentication
element.documentation: Every user is uniquely identified and strongly authenticated, with multi-factor authentication for all access into the cardholder data environment.

element.name: Multi-factor authentication into the CDE
element.documentation: Example control. Replace with the process or tool that meets this requirement in your organisation.

element.name: Requirement 9: Physical access restrictions
element.documentation: Physical access to cardholder data and the systems that hold it is controlled, media is protected, and card-reading devices are inspected for tampering.

element.name: Card terminal inspection and physical security
element.documentation: Example control. Replace with the process or tool that meets this requirement in your organisation.

element.name: Requirement 10: Logging and monitoring of all access
element.documentation: All access to system components and cardholder data is logged, logs are protected, and they are reviewed at least daily.

element.name: Central audit logging and daily review
element.documentation: Example control. Replace with the process or tool that meets this requirement in your organisation.

element.name: Requirement 11: Regular security testing
element.documentation: Systems and networks are tested regularly: quarterly internal and external vulnerability scans, annual penetration tests, and tests that prove segmentation works.

element.name: Scans, penetration and segmentation tests
element.documentation: Example control. Replace with the process or tool that meets this requirement in your organisation.

element.name: Requirement 12: Information security policies and programmes
element.documentation: Policies, risk analysis, awareness training, incident response, management of third-party service providers, and confirmation of scope at least once every twelve months.

element.name: Security policy, scoping and provider management
element.documentation: Example control. Replace with the process or tool that meets this requirement in your organisation.

element.name: Payment application
element.documentation: Takes card payments from the online shop and the telephone order desk.

element.name: Card data vault
element.documentation: Swaps card numbers for tokens and holds the only stored copy.

element.name: CDE database server
element.documentation: Hosts the card data vault's database.

element.name: Card terminals
element.documentation: Card-reading devices at the telephone order desk.

element.name: Jump host
element.documentation: The only administrative route into the cardholder data environment.

element.name: Logging platform
element.documentation: Collects and stores audit logs from every in-scope system.

element.name: CDE segmentation firewall
element.documentation: Separates the cardholder data environment from the corporate network.

element.name: Corporate office network
element.documentation: Kept out of scope by segmentation; tested to prove it.

element.name: Marketing website
element.documentation: Links to the online shop but never handles card data.

element.name: Payment service provider
element.documentation: Third-party service provider that authorises payments. Its responsibilities are recorded in the written agreement and checked against its attestation of compliance every year.

element.name: Payment services agreement
element.documentation: Acknowledges the provider's responsibility for the security of the account data it handles.

element.name: Account data
element.documentation: Cardholder data (card number, name, expiry date, service code) and sensitive authentication data. Sensitive authentication data is never kept after authorisation.

element.name: Cardholder data environment
element.documentation: The people, processes and technology that store, process or transmit account data.

element.name: Connected-to and security-impacting systems
element.documentation: In scope because they connect to the cardholder data environment or could affect its security.

element.name: Out of scope
element.documentation: Isolated from the cardholder data environment by segmentation.

view.name: Six goals and twelve requirements
view.documentation: Each goal holds its requirements; under each requirement is the control that realizes it. Fill in the owner and evidence location of every control: they are what the assessor samples.

view.name: Cardholder data environment and segmentation
view.documentation: What is in scope and why: the cardholder data environment, the systems connected to it or able to affect its security, and the segmentation firewall that keeps the corporate network and marketing website out of scope. Segmentation must be proven by testing, not assumed.

view.name: Controls on in-scope systems
view.documentation: Each control and the system it is applied to. A system in scope with no control drawn to it is where an assessment finding will land.
